We have proved that the mapping \(x\to x'\) is a homomorphism of \(\mathfrak C\) onto the subalgebra \(\mathfrak C'\) of \(\mathfrak A\) consisting of all \(x'\). ON THE SINGULAR VALUES OF A PRODUCT OF COMPLETELY  
CONTINUOUS OPERATORS

By ALFRED HORN

UNIVERSITY OF CALIFORNIA, LOS ANGELES

Communicated by G. C. Evans, May 16, 1950

In this note I wish to present a theorem on the singular values of a product of completely continuous operators in Hilbert space. As an application, a simple proof of a recent result of S. H. Chang will be given. The singular values of an operator \(K\) are the positive square roots of the eigen-values of \(K^*K\), where \(K^*\) is the adjoint of \(K\).

We begin with a slight generalization of a theorem of Weyl.¹

**THEOREM 1.** *If \(H\) is a positive, symmetric, completely continuous operator whose first \(n\) eigen-values² are \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n\), then*

\[
\det [(Hy_i,y_j)]\leq \lambda_1\cdots\lambda_n
\det [(y_i,y_j)]
\]

*for any elements \(y_1,\ldots,y_n\).*

Here, \(\det [a_{ij}]\) denotes the determinant of the \(n\)th order matrix with elements \(a_{ij}\). Weyl's elegant proof uses an appeal to the theory of \(n\)-tensors. A straightforward proof may be given by using the relation

\[
(Hy_i,y_j)=\sum_k\lambda_k(y_i,x_k)(x_k,y_j),
\]

where the \(x_k\) form a *complete ortho-normal set*.

L51@P4: Completely continuous operators on a Hilbert space or even on a
L52@P4: Banach space have received considerable attention in the last fifty years.
L53@P4: Their study was usually confined to special completely continuous
L54@P4: operators or to the discovery of properties common to all of them (for
L55@P4: instance, that every such operator admits a proper invariant subspace).
L56@P4: On the other hand, interest in spaces of completely continuous
L57@P4: operators is comparatively new. Some results of this type may be found
L58@P4: implicit in the early work of E. SCHMIDT. Other results are "generally
L59@P4: known" and cannot be found explicitly in print. One of the interesting
L60@P4: and relatively new results states that modulo the language of BANACH
L61@P4: (that is, up to equivalence) the space of all operators on a Hilbert space f>
L62@P4: is the second conjugate of the space of all completely continuous operators
L63@P4: on f>.
L64@P4: The study of spaces of completely continuous operators on a perfectly
L65@P4: general Banach space involves many difficulties. Some stem, for instance,
L66@P4: from the unsolved problem whether a completely continuous operator
L67@P4: on a perfectly general Banach space is always approximable in bound by
L68@P4: operators of finite rank. The answer is affirmative in all the special Banach
L69@P4: spaces considered. An affirmative answer to the above problem is the
L70@P4: ultimate desideratum - it ~ould simplify the theory considerably. A
L71@P4: negative answer, however, would be equally interesting (although for
L72@P4: us not so useful), since it would settle negatively the open "basis problem".
L73@P4: (The range of a completely continuous operator A may be always assumed
L74@P4: to lie in a separable Banach space; the last must not have a basis whenever A is not approximable in bound by operators of finite rank.)
L75@P4: However, at this stage of the game it is possible - and quite timelyto present a reasonable theory of spaces of completely continuous operators
L76@P4: on a Hilbert space. That is precisely what we plan to accomplish. For the
L77@P4: sake of simplicity we shall ignore the fact that fragments of the results
L78@P4: which we are about to present may be carried over in a straightforward
L79@P4: manner to completely continuous operators on an arbitrary Banach space.
L80@P4: The setting for our discussion is a complex Hilbert space f>; we
L81@P4: denote by Q{ the algebra of all operators on f>. The Banach spaces considered herein are made up of completely continuous operators on f>,
L82@P4: and the norm 0( (A) of an operator A is in general different from its
L83@P4-5: bound II A II. It turns out that the most important spaces are also the VI Preface
L84@P5: interesting ones; everyone of such spaces g(J is also a two-sided ideal in
L85@P5: the algebra Qt, and the norm on g(J satisfies the extra condition
L86@P5: cx(XA Y) ~ IIXIIIIYII cx(A)
L87@P5: for A E g(J and X, Y in Qt. Motivated by the above considerations we are
L88@P5: led to the study of norm-ideals of completely continuous operators on
L89@P5: a Hilbert space.
L90@P5: For some reason, spaces of completely continuous operators have
L91@P5: received little attention in the literature, too little when one considers the
L92@P5: rapid and significant progress of the operator theory in the last few
L93@P5: decades. It is hoped therefore that this not too pretentious presentation
L94@P5: will induce the interested reader to further investigations in this promising field.
L95@P5: Those familiar with the contributions of JOHN VON NEUMANN will
L96@P5: no doubt recognize here the influence of some of his work. It is to his
L97@P5: memory that this monograph is dedicated.
